content.title: About
content.content: Cheese‑free thin crust pizza is a variation of the classic pizza that replaces traditional cheese with sauce, vegetables, and spices. The thin crust gives a crisp texture, while the lack of cheese makes it lighter and suitable for those with lactose intolerance.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Thin crust originated in Naples in the 19th century and quickly spread worldwide.
Without cheese, the flavor of the tomato sauce and fresh toppings shines through.
Cheese‑free pizza is often featured in vegan menus, sometimes using plant‑based cheese alternatives.
Thin crust dough is made from simple ingredients: flour, water, yeast, salt, and olive oil.
In Italy, a cheese‑less pizza is sometimes called “pizza bianca” (white pizza), though it traditionally lacks tomato sauce.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: Skipping cheese reduces saturated fat content, which is beneficial for cardiovascular health.

items.title: Rich in vegetables
items.content: Tomatoes, peppers, mushrooms and other toppings provide vitamin C, potassium and antioxidants.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Thin crust contains less fiber than whole‑grain versions, but when made with whole‑grain flour it can aid regular bowel movements.

items.title: Lactose‑free
items.content: The absence of dairy makes this pizza suitable for people with lactose intolerance.

items.title: Lower calorie count
items.content: Compared with traditional cheese pizza, this version contains fewer calories, helpful for weight management.

items.title: Gluten
items.content: Thin crust is usually wheat‑based, so it is not suitable for those with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: Sodium
items.content: Tomato sauce can be salty; choose low‑sodium varieties if you need to limit salt intake.

items.title: Allergy to ingredients
items.content: Possible allergic reactions to tomatoes, peppers, mushrooms or other toppings.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: White‑flour thin crust can raise blood sugar quickly; people with diabetes may prefer whole‑grain crusts.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Enjoy the pizza hot straight from the oven or cooled. Slice into wedges and serve with extra vegetable toppings, a drizzle of olive oil, or fresh herbs. Vegans can add plant‑based cheese or a nut‑based sauce for extra richness.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2‑3 days. Reheat in the oven or skillet to restore crispness. Freeze in bags at –18 °C for up to 2 months; thaw in the refrigerator before reheating.
